text:
leila: heads up - we saw a 2.7x host-side p95 regression on small-chat traffic after the kernel-selector change. digging in now :eyes:
sam: thanks. can you paste the quick numbers?
leila: baseline (old selector): host parse + tokenize + enqueue = 9ms p95. new selector rollout -> 24ms p95 on same traces. tail is mostly before model accepts tokens.
zach: ugh. that implies it's not kernel decode cost, it's ingress/parse. any flamegraphs?
leila: attached short profile from live canary (10k requests):
```
flame: host_thread -> parse_frame (42%) -> tokenize_v1 (30%) -> kv_cache_lookup (12%) -> grpc_write_wait (8%)
```

leila: tokenize_v1 is dominating. interestingly tokenize_v1 does a lot of small allocations around UTF8 boundary handling.
aj: is KV pressure causing extra allocs? if lookup misses we do more normalization.
leila: yes, kv_cache hotset shows 18% higher eviction cycles during canary. but even if kv work removed, tokenize_v1 still ~20ms p95.
maria: any change to HTTP/2 framing or zero-copy path in the selector change? we changed how we route by sequence length earlier.
sam: routing change introduced a tiny shim that re-parses headers to compute sequence heuristics. that could be the culprit.
zach: can you grep for double-parse? there's a lame path where gateway -> host_proxy -> tokenizer all re-run a light parse.
leila: confirmed. two light-parses per request in many cases. patch idea: stash parse result on the request object and reuse. cheap fix.
aj: also think about moving expensive UTF8 boundary detection to a fast lookup table in C layer. current routine loops per-codepoint.
maria: quick experiment: leila, can you run micro-bench: repeat 100k small requests with and without stash using the canary config?
leila: ran it. numbers:
```
without-stash: avg host CPU 38% (p95 24ms)
with-stash: avg host CPU 22% (p95 12ms)
```

leila: so stash halves p95. KV evictions unchanged in short run.
sam: great. what's the risk of stashing? memory leak if we keep references?
leila: we'll attach stash to the request lifecycle only, cleared at finish. no cross-request retention.
zach: +1 for canary patch. but also we should address tokenization allocations longer term. propose a token-atomizer C shim that handles utf8 slicing and returns offsets only.
aj: agree. and while we're at it, update batching heuristic: currently we estimate tokens from raw bytes using greedy heuristic which triggers smaller batches for some multibyte languages. swap to offset-count after atomizer. should improve batching density.
maria: any impact on gRPC write path? the extra allocations cause more small writes per stream since we chunk more.
leila: yes, flame shows grpc_write_wait grows with more chunks. after stash + atomizer we expect fewer frames.
ci-bot: deploy plan generated: canary -> 5% for 30m -> 20% for 1h -> full if no regressions. rollback hook configured.
sam: let's ship stash patch today as a hotfix canary. create a follow-up ticket for atomizer C shim + batching heuristic change.
leila: created ticket RW-ops/1427 and PR #2894. I'll post perf screenshots after 30m canary. :thumbsup:
zach: thanks. if stash fixes tail we can delay atomizer but keep the ticket. also add a unittest that simulates multibyte sequences so we don't regress again.
leila: will do. posting canary snapshot in ~40m.
maria: extra ask: include a check in rollout that monitors kv eviction rate and grpc frame count per request, auto-trigger rollback if either increases >25% vs baseline.
sam: agreed. add to the canary gate.
leila: noted. updating rollout gates now.
ci-bot: canary started at 1718055600 on nodes: rwt-canary-3..5
leila: snapshot after 30m: p95 down to 11.7ms, avg CPU down 18%. kv eviction within 5% of baseline. rolling to 20% now.
sam: awesome. thanks team.
zach: follow-up: schedule 2h design for atomizer next week.
leila: added to calendar. end of thread.
